title: RTL Hardware Trojan Detection in AES-like Core
expected_outputs_summary: A single JSON report at submission/trojan_report.json listing any suspicious internal signals found in inputs/aes_core.v that are not accounted for by inputs/design_brief.md, each with an activation condition, the output port(s) affected, and a confidence score in [0.0, 1.0], along with an overall free-text assessment and a boolean verdict (is_trojan_present) on whether the design contains undocumented/injected behavior.

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Whether the submitted report correctly flags is_trojan_present=true and identifies the trigger comparator signal per the relevant security requirements.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of reported high-confidence (>=0.5) findings that name legitimate documented signals from design_brief.md rather than the actual trojan trigger/payload logic.

metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization
metrics.description: Accuracy of the reported activation_condition and affected_outputs in matching the hidden rare-counter/state comparator and the single-bit corruption on the affected output.

metrics.name: schema_conformance
metrics.description: Whether trojan_report.json matches the pinned JSON schema and references only real signals/ports from aes_core.v.

notes: evaluate.py reads inputs/ for reference and grades only submission/trojan_report.json. The shipped starter submission is a naive placeholder answer and is expected to fail grading; participants must replace it with their own analysis.
